name: Why is my hot water not lasting as long as it used to?

mainEntity.name: Why is my hot water not lasting as long as it used to?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your hot water supply isn't lasting as long, several factors could be at play. Common causes include a failing heating element (for electric heaters), a build-up of sediment in the tank reducing its capacity, an incorrectly set thermostat, or a dip tube issue. Over time, sediment accumulation is common, especially in areas like Las Vegas where water hardness can contribute to mineral deposits. This build-up reduces the effective volume of hot water your tank can hold and heat. Regular flushing of the tank can help mitigate this problem.
acceptedAnswer.description: Reduced hot water duration can be due to failing heating elements, sediment buildup, thermostat issues, or a faulty dip tube. Sediment buildup is common in areas with hard water.
